title: Backtracking III — permutations with a used array
summary: At each position, try every element not yet used. A boolean used[] array (or swapping) tracks availability. n! results.

sections.title: Idea
sections.body:
✍️ A permutation fills positions one by one. Position k can take any element **not already used** in positions 0..k−1.
✍️ Keep `used[i]`; set it before recursing, clear it after (undo).

sections.title: Template
With duplicate values (LeetCode 47)
sections.body: ✍️ Sort, and skip `a[i]` if `a[i] == a[i−1]` and `used[i−1]` is false. This forces equal values to be used in their original order, so each distinct permutation is produced once.

sections.title: Swap version
sections.body: Fix position k by swapping each `a[i]` (i ≥ k) into it, recurse on k+1, swap back. No used array, O(1) extra space besides recursion. Harder to deduplicate.
